description: Four delay taps in series clocked from a beat input, each with a note length, level, pan and feedback of its own, and a multimode filter on the way into the delay line

params.text: Picks the filter: off, low pass, high pass, band pass or notch
Sets the cutoff of the filter the signal passes through on its way into the delay line
Sets the resonance of the filter the signal passes through on its way into the delay line
Sets the level of that tap in the delayed mix
Sets the position of that tap between the left and right outputs
Sets how much of that tap is fed back into the delay line
Sets the length of that tap as a note value, off, two bars, a bar, a half, a quarter, an eighth, a sixteenth or a thirty-second, counted on from where the tap before it landed
Crossfades between the unfiltered input and the sum of the four taps

inputs.text: The clock the note lengths are measured against, one edge to the next counting as a quarter note
The left input, and the source for both sides when the right input is empty
Adds to the filter cutoff knob, 5V covering the whole of the knob's range and -5V closing the filter

outputs.text: The left output, the dry input and the delayed taps mixed by Mix
The right output, the dry input and the delayed taps mixed by Mix

notes: a tap set to Off is skipped, and the taps after it are measured from where the last sounding tap landed
all four Delay knobs come up at Off, so a new module passes the input through unchanged until at least one tap is set to a note length
the tap lengths are measured from the clock at Beat, and are recalculated on each edge of it; with that jack empty they are left at the length the module started with

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
